criteria.evidence: Doc holds only '## Directional intent' and '## Agent intent (ICE)'. No Benefit hypothesis, Boundary (In / Out / Never), Guiding rules or Functionalities sections.
criteria.fix: Add Benefit hypothesis (who it serves, what it delivers, how we will know), Boundary with In/Out/Never each explained, capability-specific Guiding rules each with a reason, and a Functionalities list with one explained line each linked to its spine node.

criteria.evidence: 'Directionally it will broadly own the win-back count and its comparison over time' and 'it stops short of finding abandoned carts or sending reminders'
criteria.fix: The why is given for the capability as a whole, but the scope lines have no per-line reasons. State in each boundary and rule line why the edge exists, e.g. why 'before reminders started' needs a baseline count and who captures it.

criteria.evidence: The Directional intent is one long flowing paragraph: 'This is about knowing whether the effort to win back abandoned carts is actually working. It counts the abandoned carts...'
criteria.fix: Break the paragraph into discrete points under the guided sections (benefit hypothesis, In, Out, Never, rules). Keep the Goal and Fails-if lines as they are.

criteria.evidence: Capability says 'Directionally it will broadly own the win-back count'; the parent domain already holds guiding rules, scope in/out and a capability line saying 'counts the reminded carts that end in an order and the sales they win back, month by month'.
criteria.fix: Add detail the domain lacks: precise definition of a reminded cart that counts as won back (time window after reminder, attribution), the pre-reminder baseline method, the month boundaries, and the functionalities.

criteria.evidence: 'without counting reminded carts that turn into orders, nobody can tell whether fewer sales are being lost or whether reminders are just noise.'
criteria.fix: The what and why are clear, but the edges and parts are not. A stranger cannot say what the capability contains, what it must never do, or how it is proved. Add the missing guided sections so the node can be explained alone.
